summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg and University of Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard Divinity School (from around 1988).

Elizabeth A. Cecil works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald and held posts at Leiden University (~2016–2018) and Florida State University (~2019).

Elizabeth De Michelis is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1996–2001). She held posts at Cambridge, serving as director in 2000, and at the University of Oxford.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Harunaga Isaacson and completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

Elizabeth Errington works in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, and served as curator of South and Central Asian pre-Islamic coins at the British Museum from 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury by 1994 and served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and held posts at Westminster College (~1993–1996) and the University of Birmingham (~2017).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978). She held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1982–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Supervised by Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, she held an instructor post at Amherst College (1998–1999) and a post at Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who served as director at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar in history/archaeology and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University under the supervision of Bozena Werbart, with co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven works in Indology and history/archaeology. She held positions at the Kern Institute (attested 2003) and on an editorial board at Leiden University (attested 2018).
Elliot M. Stern is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, earning PhDs attested in 1988 and 1998.

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history who earned his MA and PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. He served as associate professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1987–2015) and held visiting posts at Harvard and Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held academic posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford (attested 1989).
Elvin A. Kabat studied at Columbia University (~1933–1937) and held academic posts at Cornell University (~1938–1941) and Columbia University (~1941–2000).

Emanuel Sarkisyanz was a scholar of history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and University of Chicago (PhD ~1948–1952), and served as head of political science at Heidelberg University in 1967.
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist who held posts as Pandit at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and served at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937) and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara (attested 1939).
